answered.sql: SELECT system_name FROM Systems WHERE system_id IN (SELECT system_id FROM It_Support_Specialists_Systems GROUP BY system_id HAVING COUNT(it_specialist_id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM It_Support_Specialists))

candidates.meaning: List all systems that each support specialist works with.
candidates.sql: SELECT s.name, GROUP_CONCAT(sys.system_name) AS systems FROM It_Support_Specialists s JOIN It_Support_Specialists_Systems iss ON s.id = iss.it_specialist_id JOIN Systems sys ON iss.system_id = sys.system_id GROUP BY s.id, s.name

candidates.meaning: List all systems that each support specialist works with, including duplicates.
candidates.sql: SELECT s.system_name, i.name FROM It_Support_Specialists i JOIN It_Support_Specialists_Systems iss ON i.id = iss.it_specialist_id JOIN Systems s ON iss.system_id = s.system_id

candidates.meaning: For each support specialist, list the systems they work with, including duplicates and showing the specialist's name.
candidates.sql: SELECT i.name, s.system_name FROM It_Support_Specialists i JOIN It_Support_Specialists_Systems iss ON i.id = iss.it_specialist_id JOIN Systems s ON iss.system_id = s.system_id

candidates.meaning: List all unique systems that each support specialist works with, without duplicates.
candidates.sql: SELECT i.name, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT s.system_name) AS systems FROM It_Support_Specialists i JOIN It_Support_Specialists_Systems iss ON i.id = iss.it_specialist_id JOIN Systems s ON iss.system_id = s.system_id GROUP BY i.name
